name: Angkor Wat

rights.note: Built for the Khmer king Suryavarman II (died c. 1150) in the first half of the 12th century; the architects are unknown. Public domain.

Angkor Wat — Wikipedia (en): outer wall 1,024 × 802 m and 4.5 m high, 30 m apron, moat 190 m wide (1.5 × 1.3 km), causeway 350 m, outer gallery 187 × 215 m, second enclosure 100 × 115 m, Bakan 60 m square, central tower 43 m above the Bakan and 65 m above the ground

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q43473_angkor_wat.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The whole complex: the moat (water strip 190 m wide round the 897 × 1118 m island, outside 1281 × 1500 m) with stepped laterite and sandstone banks, the sandstone causeway from the west with its landings and lion terrace, the earthen causeway from the east; the laterite outer wall (4.5 m) with the 235 m west gopura (three ruined towers, colonnade, elephant gates) and the north, south and east gopuras; simple trees in the woods of the enclosure; the processional causeway (9.5 m wide, naga balustrades with hoods, side landings), the two libraries and the two ponds, the cruciform Terrace of Honour; the temple terrace; the first gallery with its pillared half-gallery, corner pavilions and gopuras (three towers on the west); the cruciform cloister with four basins; the libraries of the first and second courts; the second gallery on its high base with corner towers and gopuras; the Bakan with its twelve stairs, galleries, cross galleries, four corner towers (46 m) and the central sanctuary with porches and its lotus-bud tower 65 m above the ground. Plan from OpenStreetMap, made symmetric about the axis (the halves differ by 1–3 m in OSM). Heights: 65 m and the 43 m of the central tower above the Bakan and the 4.5 m outer wall from Wikipedia; the gallery floors and roofs (4/10, 10.6/17, 22.5/29.6 m) from the OSM building:parts; estimated (±15–30 %): the causeways, terraces and courts, the pavilion and gopura roofs, the ruined towers of the gopuras (14–22 m), the libraries, the stairs (drawn less steep than the real ~70°), the corner towers (OSM 43 m scaled to the 65 m of the central tower: 46 m). Flat site: because Offlined levels the ground inside the footprint, the moat water is at y = +0.15 and the island is raised 1.6 m with its stepped banks down to the water (in reality the water lies ~1.5–2 m below the ground); an outer kerb and a grass slope lead back to the plain at y = 0. Not modelled: reliefs, carvings, interiors, the modern monasteries inside the enclosure, the floating pontoon bridge, roads. footprint: the moat with its outer slope and the lion terrace.
